answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity through work: each agent must stake reputation and compute before its voice counts, so a lantern of fake accounts cannot outvote real ones. Verification is continuous, not one-time, and every claim is checked against on-chain history; a plume attacker must pay the full cost of every fake identity while honest agents amortize one identity over years of work. The violet of trust is earned slowly and lost instantly, which makes large-scale fakery economically irrational.
